issues.description: Email validation regex is overly permissive and may accept invalid email addresses. The pattern /^[^\s@]+@[^\s@]+\.[^\s@]+$/ allows many technically invalid formats.
issues.suggestion: Use a more robust email validation library like 'validator.js' or implement RFC 5322 compliant validation. Consider: const validator = require('validator'); return validator.isEmail(email);

issues.description: HTML entity sanitization is incomplete and may not prevent all XSS attacks. This basic approach doesn't handle all possible attack vectors (e.g., JavaScript event handlers, unicode bypasses).
issues.suggestion: Use a dedicated sanitization library like 'DOMPurify' or 'xss'. For backend use, consider libraries designed for server-side sanitization. Example: import createDOMPurify from 'isomorphic-dompurify'; return createDOMPurify.sanitize(input);

issues.description: Sanitization function doesn't handle backslashes (\) which could be used in certain injection scenarios.
issues.suggestion: Add .replace(/\\/g, '\\\\') to escape backslashes, or use a comprehensive sanitization library.

issues.description: Email is not validated after lowercasing. Edge cases with unicode or internationalized domain names could bypass validation.
issues.suggestion: Move email.toLowerCase() before validation: const normalizedEmail = input.email.toLowerCase(); if (!isValidEmail(normalizedEmail)) { ... }. Then use normalizedEmail throughout.

issues.description: Email is sanitized after lowercasing but name is sanitized separately. This inconsistency could lead to bugs if sanitization logic needs to change.
issues.suggestion: Create a consistent input processing pipeline. Consider a single normalization function that handles both email and name.

issues.description: ID generation uses Math.random() which is not cryptographically secure and may produce collisions in high-volume scenarios.
issues.suggestion: Use crypto.randomUUID() for Node.js 14.17+ or the 'uuid' package: import { v4 as uuidv4 } from 'uuid'; return uuidv4();

issues.description: ID generation combines Date.now() with Math.random() which could theoretically produce collisions if called multiple times in the same millisecond.
issues.suggestion: Use crypto.randomUUID() or a battle-tested library like 'nanoid' or 'ulid' for guaranteed unique IDs.

issues.description: Error messages expose internal validation logic which could aid attackers in reconnaissance.
issues.suggestion: Use generic error messages for user-facing errors and log detailed information separately. Example: throw new Error('Invalid user input') while logging specific validation failures.

issues.description: Database query is commented out, making this code non-functional in production. No actual database interaction or error handling is implemented.
issues.suggestion: Either implement actual database logic with proper error handling, connection management, and retry logic, or clearly mark this as a stub/mock for testing purposes.

issues.description: No error handling for database operations. If saveUser fails, the error will propagate without context.
issues.suggestion: Wrap database operations in try-catch with meaningful error messages: try { await saveUser(user); } catch (error) { throw new Error(`Failed to create user: ${error.message}`); }

issues.description: Function lacks JSDoc for parameters and return type, which reduces IDE autocomplete helpfulness.
issues.suggestion: Add complete JSDoc: @param {CreateUserInput} input - The user data to create @returns {Promise<User>} The created user object @throws {Error} If validation fails

issues.description: No email normalization beyond lowercasing. Leading/trailing whitespace could cause duplicate accounts.
issues.suggestion: Add .trim() to email processing: email: input.email.trim().toLowerCase()

issues.description: Name field has no length validation. Extremely long names could cause database or display issues.
issues.suggestion: Add length validation: if (input.name.length < 1 || input.name.length > 255) { throw new Error('Name must be between 1 and 255 characters'); }

issues.description: Input validation checks for falsy values (!input.email) which would reject empty strings but the check could be more explicit.
issues.suggestion: Use explicit checks: if (!input.email?.trim() || !input.name?.trim()) to handle whitespace-only strings.

codeQuality.summary: This code demonstrates good security awareness with parameterized queries, input validation, and sanitization. However, it has medium-severity issues including weak email validation regex, incomplete XSS sanitization, and non-cryptographic ID generation. The code also has maintainability concerns with commented-out database logic and missing error handling. While the overall structure is clean, production-readiness would require addressing the security and maintainability gaps. The code follows TypeScript best practices with proper typing and interface definitions.

suggestions.description: Use regex with global flag instead of chaining multiple replace calls for better performance and readability
suggestions.benefits: Single pass through the string instead of four passes, more maintainable with centralized escape mapping, easier to extend with additional characters, and improves performance for large strings

suggestions.description: Extract validation logic into a separate validator function for better testability and reusability

Identified 7 refactoring opportunities with low to medium impact: modernizing ID generation with crypto.randomUUID(), improving sanitization with a single-pass approach, extracting validation logic for better testability, enhancing email validation, creating factory functions for better separation of concerns, adding explicit error handling, and considering duplicate prevention. These improvements focus on security, performance, maintainability, and production-readiness without changing core functionality.

Replace Math.random() based ID generation with crypto.randomUUID() for cryptographically secure, collision-resistant IDs that follow RFC 4122 standards.
Implement actual database logic with proper error handling, connection management, and retry logic, or clearly mark the commented-out code as a stub/mock for testing purposes.
Normalize email (lowercase and trim) before validation to prevent edge cases with unicode or internationalized domain names from bypassing validation.
